slides.texte_overlay:
7 office tricks that feel
like playing on easy mode
Arrive ten minutes before your manager on Mondays. Those quiet minutes are when the best informal chats happen, and you start the week a step ahead.
Ask for feedback mid-project, not after. "Am I heading in the right direction?" Correcting early saves you from redoing everything at the last minute.
Keep a running list of questions instead of interrupting. Then ask them all in one short chat. Your colleagues will love you for respecting their focus.
Learn how decisions really get made. Who needs to say yes, who influences them. Knowing that is worth more than any official org chart on the wall.
Before: quiet in every meeting. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and fresh examples that make my ideas easy to remember and repeat.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: quiet in every meeting. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now my ideas are easy to remember.

slides.texte_overlay: Thank the people who helped you in your project update. Name them in front of the team. Shared credit makes everyone want to work with you again and again.
Block one hour a day for deep work. Phone away, notifications off. One focused hour often achieves more than a whole distracted afternoon spent jumping between tasks.
